lyo.title: Freeze-drying
lyo.p1: Freeze-drying is a preservation technique that removes water from a product by sublimation. It preserves the nutritional qualities, taste, and texture of fresh fruit.
lyo.p2: Unlike traditional techniques such as heat drying, freeze-drying is done at low temperature, keeping up to 97% of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh fruit.
lyo.p3: The result? Ultra-crunchy fruits, naturally sweet, light and easy to store, while keeping their intense flavor and nutritional benefits.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.p1: At CrunchyVita, we believe snacking can be both delicious and healthy. Our mission is to offer 100% natural snacks, with no added sugar or preservatives, made from quality fresh fruit.
mission.p2: We select our fruits carefully from certified organic farms to bring you the best of nature in every pouch.

Cookies have multiple uses: they can be used to remember your customer ID on a merchant site, the current contents of your shopping cart, the display language of the web page, an identifier used to track your browsing for statistical or advertising purposes, etc."

intro.p1: Alteora ("Alteora", "our", "we" and "us") and our partners respect your privacy. We ask that you carefully read this privacy policy to understand how your personal data is collected, processed, and retained when you use this crunchyvita website, accessible at https://www.crunchyvita.com/fr.
intro.p2: The term "personal data" refers to any information relating to a natural person that allows them to be identified, directly or indirectly, from a single piece of data or by cross-referencing several pieces of data. This includes elements such as name, address, email address, location data, online identifiers, etc.
intro.p3: All personal data collected on this website is processed under the responsibility of Alteora, a French simplified joint-stock company (SAS) with share capital of 10,000 €, registered with the Trade and Companies Register of Antibes under number 993112952, with its registered office at 1460 Chemin des Terriers, 06600 Antibes, France, and in accordance with Law No. 78-17 of January 6, 1978 on data processing, data files, and civil liberties, as amended, as well as Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of April 27, 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data.
intro.p4: Within the meaning of the regulations applicable to personal data, Alteora is therefore the data controller.

section1.title: I. How Alteora uses your personal data
section1.intro: Alteora may use your personal data for the following purposes:

items.item1: creating your customer account on this website
items.item2: managing orders for products and/or services
items.item3: carrying out the actions necessary to manage contracts, invoices, and customer relationship follow-up
items.item4: publishing and managing your reviews and/or comments left on the website
items.item5: responding to your contact requests made through our website
items.item7: offering you advertising and content tailored to you
items.item8: building a file of users, prospects, and customers
items.item10: managing any unpaid invoices and disputes

section1.p1: The data collected is necessary for the performance of the contract entered into with Alteora when you use our website to order the products and/or services available for sale on the site.
section1.p2: When you voluntarily provide us with personal data, the collection of your personal data is based on the following legitimate interest: responding more effectively to your requests for information.
section1.p3: The processing of your personal data to send you our newsletter is, however, based solely on your consent to receive our newsletter, which you can withdraw at any time. If you do not consent to receiving the newsletter, please note that this will not prevent you from creating your customer account and placing orders on our website.

legalBasis.title: Legal basis
legalBasis.intro: The processing of your data is based on:

items.item1: your consent (Article 6(1)(a) of European Regulation 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation - GDPR)) for sending the newsletter,
items.item2: the performance of a contract or pre-contractual measures (Article 6(1)(b) of the GDPR), when it comes to providing you with products or services through our site.
items.item3: Certain processing may also be based on Article 6(1)(f) of the GDPR, when the processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by Alteora, unless the fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject override those interests. This may in particular concern the improvement of our services, customer relationship management, or fraud prevention.

section2.title: II. How Alteora shares your personal data
section2.p1: Within Alteora, and with regard to each processing purpose, personal data concerning you is collected, processed, and stored by Alteora's authorized staff, solely within the scope of their respective duties, and in particular by the customer service, marketing, and IT departments.
section2.p2: We do not share personal data with other companies, organizations, or individuals, unless one of the following circumstances applies:

items.item1: sharing with prior consent: after obtaining your consent, Alteora will share the information you have authorized with the specific third parties or categories of third parties identified when your consent was collected.
items.item2: sharing with our service providers: Alteora may also disclose your information to companies that provide services for us or on our behalf. These service providers include companies that offer IT services, such as our hosting provider or our email delivery provider, delivery services for our products, or companies that carry out marketing activities on our behalf. These service providers may use your information solely to provide services on behalf of Alteora.
items.item3: in performance of a legal obligation, sharing in accordance with laws and regulations: Alteora may share your information as required by laws and regulations, in order to resolve legal disputes, or as required by judicial or administrative authorities under the law.

section2.p3: Alteora will ensure the lawfulness of any sharing of personal data through data processing clauses with the companies with which your personal data is shared, requiring them to comply with this privacy policy and to take appropriate security and confidentiality measures when processing personal data.

section3.title: III. How Alteora protects your personal data
section3.p1: Alteora attaches great importance to the security of your personal data and has adopted standard industry practices to protect your personal data and prevent unauthorized access, disclosure, use, alteration, damage, or loss of this information.
section3.p2: We have also taken appropriate precautions, through our hosting provider, to preserve the security and confidentiality of the data, and in particular to prevent it from being distorted, damaged, or disclosed to unauthorized persons.
section3.intro: Alteora also adopts the following organizational measures:

items.item1: we take reasonable and practicable measures to ensure that the personal data collected is minimal and relevant to what is necessary, given the purposes for which it is processed;
items.item2: we retain your personal data for the period strictly necessary in view of the purpose of the processing, unless the retention of your data is required or permitted by law. For example, we retain data related to the fulfillment of your orders for the period required by law for the retention of accounting records, namely a maximum of 10 years from the relevant financial year; and
items.item3: we deploy access control mechanisms to ensure that only authorized staff can access your personal data;

section3.outro: in the event of a personal data breach, Alteora will comply with the legal and regulatory requirements applicable to notifying personal data breaches to the competent supervisory authorities and/or to the data subjects concerned.

section4.title: IV. Where Alteora hosts and transfers your personal data
section4.p1: Your personal data will be hosted on the hosting infrastructure of our hosting provider, OVH, located in France.

section5.title: V. How you can manage your rights regarding your personal data
section5.p1: You have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict, and object to the processing of your personal data, as well as the right to define directives regarding the fate of your data after your death and the right to the portability of your personal data.
section5.p2: The CNIL (French Data Protection Authority) defines personal data as "any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. But because it concerns individuals, they must retain control over it."
section5.p3: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL) for France, or with a competent supervisory authority for any other Member State, depending on your habitual residence, place of work, or the place where the alleged infringement of your rights occurred, if you believe that the processing of your data does not comply with applicable law. This complaint may be lodged without prejudice to any other remedy before an administrative or judicial court, which is also a right available to you.
section5.p4: You may contact us at any time using the addresses indicated in the "How to contact us" section below in order to exercise your rights regarding your personal data under the conditions set out by applicable regulations. You must indicate which right you wish to exercise, along with all the details necessary for us to respond to your request.
section5.p5: These rights are exercised under the conditions set out by applicable regulations.

access.title: The right of access
access.body: means that you may ask us at any time to tell you whether we process personal data concerning you and, if so, to inform you which personal data is concerned as well as the characteristics of the processing carried out.

rectification.title: The right to rectification
rectification.body: means that you may ask us to rectify your personal data when it is inaccurate. You may also request that your personal data, where incomplete, be completed to the extent relevant to the purpose of the processing in question.

erasure.title: The right to erasure
erasure.intro: means that you may request the erasure of your personal data, in particular when:

items.item1: its retention is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected;
items.item2: your personal data is processed on the basis of your consent, you wish to withdraw that consent, and there is no other legal basis capable of justifying the processing;
items.item3: you have objected to the processing of your personal data and consequently wish for it to be erased;
items.item4: your personal data has been processed unlawfully;
items.item5: your personal data must be erased to comply with a legal obligation under either European Union law or French law.

limitation.title: The right to restriction
limitation.intro: means that you may ask us to restrict the processing of your personal data:

items.item1: when you contest the accuracy of your personal data, for a period allowing us to verify its accuracy;
items.item2: when, following processing established as non-compliant, you prefer restriction of the processing to complete erasure of your personal data;
items.item3: when we no longer need your personal data for the purposes of processing, but you still need it for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims;
items.item4: when you have objected to the processing of your personal data and wish for a restriction of processing for the period allowing us to verify whether the legitimate grounds you invoke are justified.

limitation.outro: Restriction of processing means that the processing of your personal data will then be limited to storage only. We will no longer carry out any other operation on the personal data concerned.

opposition.title: The right to object
opposition.body: means that you may object to the processing of your personal data when such processing is based on Alteora's pursuit of a legitimate interest. The right to object is exercised subject to demonstrating legitimate grounds relating to your particular situation. We will then stop the processing in question unless there are compelling legitimate grounds justifying its continuation in accordance with applicable regulations.

postMortem.title: The right to define directives regarding the fate of your data after your death
postMortem.body: allows you to communicate your instructions regarding the retention, erasure, and disclosure of your personal data after your death.

portability.title: The right to data portability
portability.body: means that you may ask us, under the conditions set out by applicable regulations, to receive your personal data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format, and to have it transmitted to you, or to ask us to transmit it directly to a third party of your choice where this is legally and technically possible.

section5.p6: Where we process your personal data on the basis of your consent, you also have the right to withdraw your consent at any time by contacting us at the addresses indicated in the "How to contact us" section, or by clicking on the unsubscribe link included in each of our communications.
section5.p7: However, the withdrawal of your consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before such withdrawal.

section6.title: VI. Updates to this privacy policy
section6.p1: Alteora reserves the right to modify or update this privacy policy, in whole or in part, at any time, due to changes in the regulations applicable to the protection of personal data or to the data processing carried out.
section6.p2: Any substantial modification of the privacy policy will be notified to you by email where you have provided us with a valid email address, and will be published on the website. We recommend that you regularly review this privacy policy in order to stay fully informed of our commitments regarding the security and protection of your personal data.

section7.title: VII. How to contact us
section7.p1: If you have any questions, comments, or suggestions, please contact us by visiting our contact page or by submitting them to contact@crunchyvita.com.
section7.p2: You may also write to us by post at: Alteora, 1460 Chemin des Terriers, 06600 Antibes, France.
section7.p3: If you are not satisfied with Alteora's response to a request to exercise your rights in accordance with Section V above, or if you wish to report a breach of applicable data protection regulations, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the CNIL by post (CNIL - 3 Place de Fontenoy - TSA 80715 - 75334 PARIS CEDEX 07) or on its website (www.cnil.fr), or with the data protection authority of the country in which you habitually reside or work.

ShippingPolicy.title: Shipping Policy

preparation.title: Preparation and shipping
preparation.p1: Orders placed on www.crunchyvita.com are prepared and dispatched within an indicative period of 48 business hours from validation, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays.
preparation.p2: As soon as the parcel is handed over to the carrier, the Customer receives a shipping confirmation email including, where applicable, a tracking number to follow the shipment.
preparation.p3: During periods of high activity, the preparation time may exceptionally be extended to 72 business hours.
preparation.p4: Delivery is organized via the Boxtal platform, which allows CrunchyVita to select a partner carrier according to the chosen delivery method, destination, and options available at the time of order. Orders may be delivered to the Customer's home, workplace, or a pickup point, depending on the option selected during purchase.

absence.title: In case of absence
absence.p1: If the Customer is absent at the time of home delivery, a delivery notice may be left by the carrier, or the Customer may be contacted according to the carrier's procedures.
absence.p2: Where the delivery method allows it, the Customer may also provide delivery instructions to the carrier.
absence.p3: If the parcel is not collected within the allotted time, especially at a pickup point, it may be returned to our warehouse.

missingInfo.title: Missing information or incomplete details
missingInfo.p1: The Customer must provide all information required for proper shipment of the order, including: full address, phone number, name, access code, floor, or any other useful delivery detail.
missingInfo.p2: In the event of an error, omission, or incomplete information preventing delivery, our company cannot be held liable for the inability to deliver the order under the planned conditions.
missingInfo.p3: The parcel may then be returned to our warehouse. The Customer must contact customer service to arrange a new shipment, which may be re-invoiced to the Customer.

issues.title: Delivery issues
issues.p1: Products are shipped at our company's risk, except in specific cases related to a Customer fault, an incorrect address, or missing information provided at the time of order.
issues.p2: Upon receipt, the Customer must check the condition of the parcel and the number of delivered products.
issues.p3: Any reservation related to delivery (damaged parcel, missing product, damaged packaging, opened parcel, etc.) must be stated precisely to the carrier or on any delivery document provided at receipt, and the Customer must keep proof.
issues.p4: Any complaint regarding delivery must be submitted within 3 working days after receipt of the products, by email to the following address:

fees.title: Shipping fees and delivery offer
fees.p1: Free delivery in France to Chronopost pickup points from 40 EUR of purchases may be offered depending on the conditions displayed on www.crunchyvita.com at the time of order. This statement currently appears in the Terms of Sale available on the site.
fees.p2: Any complaint regarding delivery must be submitted within 3 working days after receipt of the products, by email to:

ShippingPolicy.promo: Free delivery in France to pickup points from 40EUR of purchases!

returnSection.title: Returns
returnSection.p1: With our company, the customer may return the product(s) concerned (in their original condition and accompanied by all commercial documents included with the delivery).
returnSection.p2: Return shipping costs are borne by the customer, except when a product has a manufacturing defect or does not match the original order. Only the price of the returned product(s) will be refunded. The refund will be made as soon as possible and no later than 14 days after receipt of the products by our company, using the payment method chosen at purchase.
returnSection.p3: The right of withdrawal may be exercised from the time the order is placed, after the customer has received delivery of the products. The criteria are based on the original condition and a state that allows resale. The company reserves the right to refuse products that do not meet these return conditions and to send them back to the customer.

procedure.title: Return procedure
procedure.intro: To ensure optimal processing of your return, please follow the procedure below:

step1.title: 1. Contact customer service by email at contact@crunchyvita.com
step1.body: specifying the invoice number and the products concerned.

step2.title: 2. Prepare the products concerned
step2.body: in their original packaging, accompanied by the invoice.

step3.title: 3. Return the parcel to the following address:
step3.address: ALTEORA, 1460 Chemin des Terriers Building B-04 06600 Antibes.
step3.note: The parcel must be dropped off at a post office within 14 days from the date of return authorization.

procedure.outro: Upon receipt of your parcel, our quality service will verify the integrity of the return and the acceptance conditions. If the conditions are met, we will proceed with a refund or replacement and send the products within 3 to 5 working days from the time your return is taken in charge by our warehouse.

refund.title: Refund
refund.p1: Refunds are issued according to the payment method and currency used at purchase.
refund.p2: We will refund your returned item as soon as possible after its receipt. The credit to your bank account will be effective within 7 to 10 working days.

article7.body:

Computer systems and files constitute valid evidence in the relationship between Alteora and the User.

Accordingly, Alteora may validly produce, as evidence in any proceeding, the data, files, programs, records, or other elements received, sent, or stored by means of the computer systems used, on any digital or analog media, and may rely on such evidence unless a manifest error is shown.

article10.title: Article 10: Severability
article10.body: The fact that any provision of the Agreement is or becomes illegal or unenforceable shall not in any way affect the validity or enforceability of the other provisions of the Agreement.

article11.title: Article 11: Dispute Resolution
article11.body:
The conclusion, interpretation, and validity of this Agreement are governed by French law, regardless of the User's country of origin or the country from which the User accesses crunchyvita, and notwithstanding conflict of law principles.

In the event of a dispute concerning the validity, performance, or interpretation of this Agreement brought before civil courts, it shall be submitted to the exclusive jurisdiction of the French courts, to which jurisdiction is expressly granted, even in cases of summary proceedings or multiple defendants.

The User is informed that they may, in any case, resort to conventional mediation or any alternative dispute resolution method (such as conciliation) in the event of a dispute.

article12.body:
These Terms of Use are entered into for an indefinite period; the User is required to comply with them from the start of their use of the Services.

items.item1: The Service Provider guarantees that the creations are legally available and free of any third-party rights for the uses contemplated under the Contract.

article16.title: Article 16. Insurance
article16.p1: Each Party agrees to maintain, for the entire duration of the Contract, with a reputable and solvent insurance company, an insurance policy covering damage that may occur to its property and personnel, as well as a professional liability policy, so as to cover the financial consequences of any bodily, material, or intangible damage for which it may be liable, caused by any event attributable to its employees and/or any partner companies during the performance of the Contract.

article17.title: Article 17. Confidentiality
article17.p1: Each Party agrees, on its own behalf and on behalf of its employees and partner companies, to preserve the confidentiality of the confidential information exchanged (the "Confidential Information"). exclusions.item3: were legitimately obtained from a third party not bound by a confidentiality obligation;

commitments.item1: to apply to the Confidential Information the same protective measures it applies to its own confidential information;

commitments.item3: not to disclose, publish, or transmit the Confidential Information to third parties, in any form whatsoever, without the other Party's prior written consent;

article18.title: Article 18. Non-Solicitation
article18.p1: Each Party agrees, unless otherwise agreed in writing, not to directly or indirectly make employment offers to a staff member of the other Party who has worked on the Services covered by this Contract, or to hire such person in any capacity whatsoever. article21.title: Article 21. Governing Law and Jurisdiction
article21.p1: The Contract is governed by French law. The parties expressly agree that the Vienna Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods of April 11, 1980 does not apply to the Contract.
article21.p2: In the event of a dispute between the Parties, they will attempt to reach an amicable resolution within thirty days of notification of the dispute by the requesting Party to the other Party by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt.
article21.p3: Failing an amicable resolution between the Parties, the dispute will be submitted to the competent Commercial Court.

article23.title: Article 23. Subcontracting

autonomieClauses.title: b) Severability
autonomieClauses.p1: If any provision of these GTC, or its application to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, such invalidity will not affect the other provisions or applications of these GTC, which will remain in effect independently of the provision held invalid. To this end, the provisions of these GTC are deemed severable.

notification.title: c) Notice
notification.p1: Any notice must be made in writing and either delivered by hand, sent by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, or served by extrajudicial process to the address indicated in the order.

langue.title: d) Language of the Contract
langue.p1: The Contract is drafted in French. A translation into a foreign language may be provided for informational purposes. In the event of any discrepancy, only the French version will be binding between the Parties.
